header.name: Usable Security and Privacy
header.description: This course will examine how to design for security and privacy from a user-centered perspective by combining insights from computer systems, human-computer interaction (HCI), and public policy. Topics will include usable authentication, user-centered web security, anonymity software, privacy notices, security warnings, and data-driven privacy tools in domains ranging from social media to the Internet of Things.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Understand the key concepts in Security and HCI required for developing Usable Security and Privacy applications/services

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Develop ability to explain limitation of key approaches/solutions in the domain of Usability and Security

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Critique and evaluate the effectiveness of proposed solutions by conducting user studies

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Design, develop and implement specific solution(s) to enhance Usability of Security/Privacy Solutions

lecture_topics: Fundamentals of Human-Computer Interaction: users, usability, tasks, and cognitive models
Strategies for Secure Interaction Design: authority, guidelines for interface design
Usable Authentication: authentication mechanisms, biometrics, two-factor authentication
Usable Privacy models: Privacy settings, personal data sharing, data inference
Web Security: Online Tracking and Surveillance

weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Course Project: A choice of projects will be provided. Students who have their own ideas for projects should discuss them with the instructors early in the quarter.
